finding.claim: The verifier cache only applies exp/nbf/maxAge limits when the payload has a numeric iat. A signed token with exp but no iat is cached for the full cacheTTL (default 10 minutes) and is accepted from the cache after it has expired.
finding.source: A validly signed token that has `exp` but no `iat`, presented to a verifier with caching enabled. The attacker only needs to replay a token they hold, for example a short-lived token that has since expired.
finding.sink: Cache-hit return in verify() at verifier.js:376-377, which returns the payload as authenticated without re-running verifyToken().

trace.note: On first successful verification, cacheSet() stores the payload.
hasIat is false when iat is missing, so the whole block that reads exp, nbf and maxAge is skipped.
cacheValue[2] is 0, so it is set to clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, which ignores exp.
Later calls look the token up in the cache.
With min == 0 and now <= max the check passes, so the expired token is returned. The decoder and verifyToken() are never run.

finding.guards_checked: validateClaimDateValue only runs on a cache miss. The cache TTL is capped at cacheTTL (600s default), so the window is bounded, but a token with exp = T+60s stays accepted until about T+600s. nbf is ignored in the same way. A token that has iat is handled correctly.

finding.claim: Claim validators for allowedIss, allowedAud, allowedSub, allowedJti, allowedNonce and maxAge are silently skipped when the claim is absent from the token. A validly signed token that omits `iss` or `aud` passes an issuer or audience restriction unless the integrator also lists the claim in requiredClaims.
finding.source: A validly signed token from the same key, for example one issued for another service or purpose, that omits iss, aud or iat.
finding.sink: verifyToken() returns the payload as accepted with no iss/aud check applied (verifier.js:304-323).

trace.note: requiredClaims is the only place absence is enforced, and it is optional.
`if (!(claim in payload)) continue` skips the validator when the claim is missing.
The aud, iss and other validators are registered only to check values that are present.

finding.guards_checked: Signature and algorithm checks still apply. requiredClaims can close the gap but is not defaulted from the allowed* options. The same applies to exp: tokens with no exp never expire unless exp is listed in requiredClaims.

finding.claim: Fail-open when the verifier key is empty. If the key option is '' or null with a non-none algorithms list such as ['HS256'], the signature check is skipped. A forged token with a valid alg header and an empty signature is accepted.
finding.source: An attacker-built token such as base64url({alg:HS256}).payload. (empty signature). The precondition is a misconfigured key, for example an unset or empty SECRET environment variable.
finding.sink: verifyToken() accepts the payload without any signature verification.

trace.note: typeof '' is 'string' and typeof null is 'object', so the key type check passes.
`key &&` is falsy, so key detection and preparation are skipped and the user-supplied algorithms list is kept.
hasKey is false (empty string is falsy).
`!hasKey && signature` is false because the signature is empty, so no error is thrown.
`signature && !verifySignature(...)` short-circuits on the empty signature, and header.alg HS256 is in allowedAlgorithms.

finding.guards_checked: With no algorithms option, allowedAlgorithms is [] and every alg is rejected, so that configuration is safe. A non-empty key requires a signature (line 274). A key function path checks the resolved key. The createVerifier constructor does not reject an empty key.
